organizer_domain_provenance: girlup.org first-party, same as the Teen Advisor and Clubs records; programme contact AWARDS@GIRLUP.ORG is on the same domain. Same crawler caveat: girlup.org 403s server-side fetchers and required a browser session. It is a .org and will fail looksOfficial().

age_range.quote: Girl Up Project Awards allow anyone between the ages of 13-24 to apply for a cause they are passionate about

prerequisites: A project idea or a planned event needing funding; club events qualify
financial_aid: n/a — this is itself a grant
selection_process: Application for funding, administered by region. Not described in detail on the official page.
award_or_output: Funding of up to $1,000 USD to deliver the applicant's own project or event
latest_verified_cycle: 2025 round — closed for MENA, Canada, South Asia & the Pacific and Europe as of the page state on 2026-08-21
leadership_evidence: GENUINE, AND THE LOW AGE FLOOR IS WHAT MAKES IT VALUABLE. This is a cash grant of up to $1,000 awarded to a young person to execute a project of their own design, open from age 13 and open worldwide. Winning one produces exactly the artefact ORYN's catalogue lacks: a 15-year-old who can say they proposed a project, won external funding for it, and delivered it — with a budget figure attached. Girl Up's own alumni stories describe awardees launching things like a girl-centred hackathon in Brasil, which is the kind of concrete outcome a counselor can interrogate. HONEST LIMITS: the official page describes no selection criteria, no cohort size and no reporting requirement, so the selectivity signal is unknown; and unlike the Teen Advisor role there is no ongoing responsibility — it funds one project, it does not confer a position. Best used as a funding mechanism for a student who already has an idea, particularly one who founded a Girl Up Club and needs money to run something through it.

research_notes: WHY CURRENT_CYCLE_NOT_PUBLISHED: the official page states plainly that 'The 2025 Project Award application is now closed for youth in MENA, Canada, South Asia & the Pacific, and Europe' and redirects three other regions into camps and hackathons instead. No 2026 or 2027 round is announced. Closed does not mean discontinued — but there is no open cycle to record, and no next date, so deadline and application_open_date are null. NOTE THE STALENESS PATTERN: this is the third Girl Up page in this lane carrying an out-of-date cycle label (the Teen Advisors overview page still advertises a January deadline for a superseded cohort). Girl Up's site is actively maintained but its programme pages lag their actual cycles, so ORYN should re-verify Girl Up records more often than most, and should never surface a Girl Up deadline without a fresh check. DELIBERATE NULLS: selection_process, duration, application_url, cohort size — none published. GENDER ELIGIBILITY NOT VERIFIED: the page says 'anyone between the ages of 13-24' with no gender criterion stated, in contrast to the Teen Advisor role which explicitly requires identifying as a girl, woman or gender expansive youth. I have not asserted that Project Awards are open to all genders, because 'anyone' in the context of Girl Up's mission is ambiguous and the page does not resolve it.

canonical_name: GençBizzTech — Bilim ve Teknoloji Temelli Lise Girişimcilik Programı
organizer: Genç Başarı Eğitim Vakfı (JA Türkiye) in partnership with Türkiye İş Bankası
organizer_domain_provenance: gencbizztech.org is the programme's own dedicated site, and the parent foundation's site gencbasari.org lists GençBizzTech in its programme portfolio alongside GençBizz, JuniorBizz and JA StartUP — I read both directly, so the programme-to-foundation link is confirmed from both ends. gencbasari.org additionally carries a 'Member of JA WORLDWIDE' statement. NOT YET DONE: no Ministry of National Education page fetched, although the sibling GençBizz programme is delivered under an MEB protocol. It is a .org and will fail looksOfficial().
grade_range: State science high schools only — 'Türkiye'nin 81 ilindeki devlet fen liselerinde öğrenim gören öğrencilerin katılabileceği'
prerequisites: Enrolment at a state science high school (devlet fen lisesi)
A participating teacher — teacher involvement in registration is required
A team of at least two students ('en az 2 kişiden oluşmalıdır')
Completion of at least one training module before advancing
duration: An academic-year cycle: training phase, project development, semifinal submission, then Turkey Finals
selection_process: Register with a teacher and team → form the team on the platform → complete at least one training module → develop a project and build a first prototype → submit a semifinal application → 10 finalist teams are selected for the Turkey Finals.
award_or_output: A developed science/technology venture project with a prototype; ten teams reach the Turkey Finals; the winning team earns participation in GEN-E in Latvia, described on the official site as 'Avrupa'nın en büyük girişimcilik festivali' (Europe's largest entrepreneurship festival)
latest_verified_cycle: 2026 cycle — Turkey Finals already held; 10 finalist high-school teams announced
leadership_evidence: MODERATE-TO-STRONG, WITH A HARD ACCESS GATE. Students form their own team, complete training, build a working prototype and compete through a semifinal to a national final of ten teams — so a participant can demonstrate co-founding a venture project, delivering a prototype, and (if a finalist) placing in the top ten nationally, with the winner competing at a European festival. That is real execution and team evidence, not a pitch exercise. THE GATE IS THE PROBLEM AND MUST BE STATED FIRST: eligibility is restricted to students at state science high schools (devlet fen liseleri). Students at private schools, Anatolian high schools, imam hatip or vocational schools are excluded outright, which rules out a large share of ORYN's likely Turkish users. A counselor must check school type before ever surfacing this. Teacher participation is also mandatory, so a motivated student cannot enter alone. DISTINCT FROM the 'GencBizz Lise Girisimcilik Programi' already in ORYN's catalogue — that is the general high-school entrepreneurship programme delivered across all school types under an MEB protocol; this is the science-technology track restricted to state science high schools, with a different sponsor and a different competitive structure.

CALENDAR CAVEAT: the site publishes its activity calendar as an image, so specific dates were not readable as text from the fetch — anyone re-verifying should open the calendar graphic rather than trusting the text layer.

organizer: INJAZ Al-Arab, the Regional Operating Center of JA Worldwide for the MENA region; delivered through national INJAZ member organisations
organizer_domain_provenance: injazalarab.org is the regional body's own site; I read its Our Story and Programs pages directly through a browser (the domain was blocked to server-side fetch). It self-identifies as having joined 'the global network of Junior Achievement Worldwide' in 2004, 'becoming the Regional Operating Center for the MENA region', which places it in the same federation as JA Europe and Türkiye's Genç Başarı Eğitim Vakfı. National members run their own domains (injaz-lebanon.org, injaz-eldjazair.org). It is a .org and will fail looksOfficial().
eligible_countries: MENA region — INJAZ states it operates in 13 countries; the list is not published on the pages I read
award_or_output: Progression to a national Young Entrepreneurs Competition and INJAZ's regional Young Entrepreneurs Celebration
leadership_evidence: NOT ASSESSABLE FROM VERIFIED EVIDENCE — recorded deliberately as an unresolved lead rather than dropped, because it is the only route I found into the Middle East and North Africa and ORYN's catalogue has essentially nothing there. What IS verified on INJAZ's own pages: the organisation exists, is JA Worldwide's Regional Operating Center for MENA since 2004, operates in 13 countries with 4,500+ schools, 700+ universities and 13 ministries of education, and lists 'The Company Program' among its entrepreneurship programmes. By family resemblance to JA Europe's and Young Enterprise's Company Programmes, the Company Program is very likely to involve forming a student company with elected roles — but I did not verify that for INJAZ, and I will not assert it. What is NOT verified and blocks a usable record: age or school-level eligibility, duration, dates, deadlines, cost, team size, and whether the high-school track exists in every member country.

research_notes: WHY NEEDS_REVIEW AND NOT A DROP: this is the only MENA-region entrepreneurship route surfaced in the whole lane, and the organisation itself is unambiguously verified — it is only the programme's eligibility that is unresolved. Recording it as an explicit unknown is more useful to the next researcher than deleting it. WHY IT IS NOT A VERIFIED RECORD: the regional site lists programme names without detail pages. injazalarab.org/the-company-program/ returns 'This page could not be found'. Third-party sources describe a '6-month entrepreneurship program starting from June to September, open to high school teams of 3+ members', but that description traces to INJAZ Lebanon, a single national member — and a sibling member, INJAZ El Djazair, publishes a Company Program aimed at university students under 25 instead. THE TWO NATIONAL MEMBERS DISAGREE about who the programme is for, which is precisely why no regional age range can be published. NEXT STEP FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: this cannot be one catalogue record. It has to be resolved per country against each national INJAZ member's own site, exactly as the JA Europe record notes that JA member countries publish different age rules (JA Europe 15-18 vs Young Enterprise UK 13-19) for the same federation programme.
